claims.text: The FeNiCrCoCu alloy has composition Fe33Ni32Cr11Co11Cu13.
The FeNiCrCoCu coating is supported on a single-crystal Cu matrix.
The initial coating is fully crystalline FCC.
The initial coating has high stacking-fault energy.
The initial coating contains no pre-existing amorphous regions.
Above 900 K, deformation transitions from dislocation-mediated plasticity to rapid thermally activated amorphization.
High configurational entropy fails to stabilize the lattice against shear-induced disordering above 900 K.
Amorphization causes annihilation of Shockley partials and collapse of the HCP-to-FCC stacking-fault network.
Shear localization creates a transient amorphous layer at the contact interface.
The transient amorphous layer initially increases friction through adhesive bonding.
Loss of the load-bearing crystalline structure causes catastrophic loss of wear resistance.
Lattice distortion and sluggish diffusion at high temperature facilitate rapid local disordering.
At lower temperatures, dislocation slip and twinning dominate deformation in this alloy.
At 600 K, dislocation density decreases.
The decrease in dislocation density at 600 K increases the elastic modulus.
Wear resistance remains high at 600 K because stable dislocation slip and twinning persist.
The friction coefficient exceeds 0.8 at 900 K and 1200 K.
Hardness or wear resistance drops by more than 50% at 900 K and 1200 K relative to 600 K.
HCP atom count shows a transient increase followed by a rapid decline as amorphization develops.
Total dislocation line length drops concurrently with amorphization because dislocations are starved or absorbed into the amorphous zone.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis places the transition strictly above 900 K, while the predicted outcome asserts that the amorphization-associated friction and wear changes occur at 900 K as well as 1200 K.
